stemBlocks.value: A group of 100 students estimated the mass, m grams, of a seed; the results are shown on a cumulative frequency curve rising from 0 at m = 0 to 100 at about m = 8. Using the curve, estimate (i) the median, (ii) the upper quartile, (iii) the semi-interquartile range, (iv) the number of students whose estimate is 2.8 grams or less.
Think first: Read from the cumulative frequency axis across to the curve and down for a mass; read up from the mass axis for a number of students.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p218-q06 from workbook page 218.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the cumulative frequency that locates the median and read across.

contentBlocks.value: Half of 100 is 50; draw a horizontal line from 50 to the curve and drop to the mass axis

solutionSteps.instruction: Repeat at three-quarters of the total for the upper quartile.
Read the lower quartile the same way at one quarter of the total.
Halve the interquartile range for the semi-interquartile range.
For 2.8 g or less, read upward from the mass axis to the curve.

contentBlocks.value: Go up from m = 2.8 to the curve, then across to the cumulative frequency axis

strategyBlocks.value: Convert each required statistic into a cumulative frequency (50, 75, 25 out of 100), read the matching mass off the curve, then combine the quartiles; for part (iv) read in the opposite direction, from m = 2.8 up to the curve.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) Median ≈ 3.2 g  (ii) Upper quartile ≈ 4.3 g  (iii) Lower quartile ≈ 2.3 g, so semi-interquartile range ≈ (4.3 − 2.3)/2 ≈ 1.0 g  (iv) About 38 students. (These are graph readings, so answers within about ±0.2 g and ±2 students are acceptable.)

whyThisWorks.value: On a cumulative frequency curve the vertical axis counts how many students gave an estimate at or below a mass, so a chosen count fixes a position in the ordered data and the curve converts it into a mass. That is exactly what the median and quartiles are: the values at the 50%, 25% and 75% positions. The semi-interquartile range halves the spread of the middle 50% of the data, giving a measure of spread that ignores extreme estimates.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the number of students (100) as a mass, or reading the axes the wrong way round.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the number of students (100) as a mass, or reading the axes the wrong way round.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking the quartiles at 25 and 75 on the mass axis instead of the cumulative frequency axis.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking the quartiles at 25 and 75 on the mass axis instead of the cumulative frequency axis.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to halve the interquartile range for the semi-interquartile range.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the median at the highest point of the curve instead of at half the total frequency.

examTip.value: Always draw the dashed reference lines on the graph — examiners award marks for the correct construction lines even if your reading is slightly out.
